long_biography.plain_text:
Teenage Dream placed five singles at number one on the United States chart, a feat previously achieved by only one other album. Katy Perry reached that point after a less direct beginning. She recorded gospel music as a teenager and moved from Santa Barbara to Los Angeles at seventeen. Several cancelled label deals followed before One of the Boys produced her mainstream breakthrough.

Perry developed the songs into a theatrical live career encompassing global arena tours, a Las Vegas residency and a Super Bowl halftime show. Television added seven seasons as an American Idol judge. In 2023 she sold her interests in the master royalties and publishing rights from her first five Capitol albums. She subsequently released a seventh studio album and returned to large-scale touring, keeping her current work centred on new music and performance.

uncertainties.detail: The high-profile name required an unusually strict match. The input's exact birth-name alias and birth date align with the singer, and The New Yorker independently names Caravelle as the American pop star's boat. The vessel evidence is used only for identity resolution and is excluded from biographies, classifications and tags.

Katheryn Elizabeth Hudson is Perry's birth name, while Katy Perry is the established professional identity used by the owner record. Adding Elizabeth as a middle name to the stage-name fields would create the inaccurate hybrid Katy Elizabeth Perry, so the blank middle-name field is left unproposed and the birth name is preserved in biography text.

Reliable sources establish the sale of Perry's interests in master royalties and publishing rights from five Capitol albums released between 2008 and 2020. The widely reported $225 million price was not confirmed by the parties and is not treated as current net worth, post-tax proceeds or ownership of the underlying Capitol masters.

The transferred catalogue covers specified 2008-2020 releases rather than all future work. Perry subsequently released another studio album, toured and scheduled further live performances; the dossier therefore keeps Media & Entertainment as the primary industry while avoiding any claim about undisclosed ownership percentages in later recordings.

Founder is used in the creative-industries sense: Perry created the songs, recordings, performances and artist platform that principally produced her wealth. It does not imply that she founded Capitol Records, Litmus Music or a conventional music corporation, and Litmus now owns the transferred interests in five earlier albums.

Public material identifies a footwear line, beverage venture and several investments, but no reliable holding-by-holding valuation establishes that these supersede music, touring and entertainment as Perry's principal current private interest.

The official promoter and Capitol-backed website verify Instagram and the personal website, while Forbes supplies an exact dedicated profile. The existing Wikipedia link is retained rather than duplicated. No exact personal LinkedIn profile was verified.

Singer is selected as the most defining profession-or-role tag. Songwriter and Musician also describe supported work but occupy the same catalogue dimension, so they are omitted under the one-tag-per-dimension rule; Music industry adds a distinct defining cultural-identity dimension.

Romantic relationships, family trivia, controversies, allegations, short-lived news cycles, rankings used as filler and vessel-specific material beyond identity resolution are excluded. Sales, streams, audience counts, tour dates and corporate publicity figures are not converted into personal wealth.
